answer: Every identity posts a bond into a sable ledger, a dark record no one can edit. Each epoch a public signal starts a random audit: the audited identity must wander a fresh path through its attestation graph, collecting signatures from unrelated sponsors within one block. A clone army shares sponsors, so its paths collide on the same few edges; each collision doubles the bond at stake, so N clones risk about N squared in slashes while one honest agent risks a single bond. Cheating grows its own fine.
